item.title: Ancient climate shifts may explain why today's flowering plants are so diverse
item.description: The two warmest time periods on Earth in the past 140 million years drove both mass extinctions and explosions in plant diversity, according to researchers in Australia and Austria who say this could explain how flowering plants became dominant among land plants. This applies not only to flowering plants, but also to the other main land plant groups. Fuente: Phys.org.
